Psalms 67

Read this chapter on staging

67:1For the end. Of David, a psalm of a song.

67:2Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered,
and let those hating Him flee from His presence.

67:3As smoke vanishes, let them vanish;
as wax melts before fire,
so may sinners perish before God.

67:4Let the righteous rejoice and exult before God;
let them delight in gladness.

67:5Sing to God; make music to His name.
Make a road for Him who rides upon the west—Lord is His name—
and exult before Him.
They will be troubled before Him,

67:6the Father of orphans and judge of widows,
God in His holy place.

67:7God settles those of one disposition in a house,
leading out the fettered with courage,
likewise the rebellious who dwell in tombs.

67:8God, when Thou wentest out before Thy people,
when Thou didst pass through the wilderness—Diapsalma—

67:9the earth shook, and indeed the heavens dripped
before God—this Sinai—
before the God of Israel.

67:10Thou wilt set apart willing rain, God, for Thine inheritance;
it grew weak, but Thou didst restore it.

67:11Thy living creatures dwell in it;
in Thy kindness Thou didst prepare for the poor, God.

67:12The Lord will give an utterance to those announcing good news with great power,

67:13the king of the powers of the beloved,
and for the beauty of the house to divide spoils.

67:14If you sleep between the allotted portions—
a dove’s wings plated with silver,
and its back in the green sheen of gold. Diapsalma.

67:15When the Heavenly One distinguishes kings upon it,
they will be covered with snow in Selmon.

67:16A mountain of God, a rich mountain;
a curdled mountain, a rich mountain.

67:17Why do you suppose, curdled mountains,
that this is the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell?
For indeed the Lord will dwell to the end.

67:18God’s chariot is ten-thousandfold,
thousands of flourishing ones;
the Lord is among them, in Sinai, in the holy place.

67:19Thou didst ascend on high; Thou tookest captivity captive;
Thou didst receive gifts among humankind,
and indeed the disobedient, to establish a dwelling.
Blessed is the Lord God.

67:20Blessed is the Lord day by day;
the God of our salvations will prosper our way. Diapsalma.

67:21Our God is a God of saving,
and to the Lord, the Lord, belong the exits of death.

67:22Nevertheless God will crush His enemies’ heads,
the crown of hair of those walking in their offenses.

67:23The Lord said, “I will return from Bashan;
I will return in the depths of the sea,

67:24so that your foot may be dipped in blood,
and the tongue of your dogs from enemies, from him.”

67:25Thy processions were seen, God,
the processions of my God, the King in the holy place.

67:26Rulers went first, closely followed by musicians,
amid young women beating tambourines.

67:27In assemblies bless God,
the Lord, from Israel’s springs.

67:28There is Benjamin, the younger, in ecstasy;
Judah’s rulers, their leaders,
Zebulun’s rulers, Naphtali’s rulers.

67:29Command Thy power, God;
strengthen, God, this which Thou didst accomplish for us.

67:30From Thy sanctuary over Jerusalem,
kings will bring Thee gifts.

67:31Rebuke the beasts of the reed,
the assembly of bulls among the heifers of peoples,
so that those tested by silver may not be shut out;
scatter nations that desire wars.

67:32Envoys will come from Egypt;
Ethiopia will hasten its hand toward God.

67:33Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God;
make music to the Lord. Diapsalma.

67:34Make music to God, who rides upon the heaven of heaven toward the east;
behold, He will give with His voice a voice of power.

67:35Give glory to God;
His magnificence is over Israel,
and His power in the clouds.

67:36Wondrous is God among His holy ones;
the God of Israel will give power and strengthening to His people.
Blessed is God.

Psalms 68

Read this chapter on staging

68:1For the end. Concerning those who will be changed. Of David.

68:2Save me, God,
for waters have entered as far as my soul.

68:3I was stuck in the mud of the depth, with no firm ground;
I entered the sea’s depths, and a tempest drowned me.

68:4I grew weary crying out; my throat became hoarse;
my eyes failed from hoping in my God.

68:5More numerous than the hairs on my head became those hating me without cause;
my enemies pursuing me unjustly became strong.
What I did not plunder, I was then repaying.

68:6God, Thou knewest my folly,
and my offenses were not concealed from Thee.

68:7May those waiting for Thee not be ashamed because of me,
Lord, Lord of powers;
may those seeking Thee not be embarrassed because of me,
God of Israel,

68:8for on Thine account I endured reproach;
embarrassment covered my face.

68:9I became estranged from my brothers
and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,

68:10for zeal for Thy house devoured me,
and the reproaches of those reproaching Thee fell upon me.

68:11I bowed my soul down in fasting,
and it became a reproach to me.

68:12I made sackcloth my garment,
and became a proverb to them.

68:13Those sitting in the gate talked against me,
and wine-drinkers sang about me.

68:14But I, in my prayer, turn toward Thee, Lord;
a time of favor, God, in the abundance of Thy mercy.
Hear me in the truth of Thy salvation.

68:15Save me from clay so that I may not become stuck;
may I be rescued from those hating me and from the depth of waters.

68:16Let no tempest of water drown me,
nor the depth swallow me;
let no well close its mouth over me.

68:17Hear me, Lord, for Thy mercy is kind;
according to Thine abundant compassions, look upon me.

68:18Do not turn Thy face away from Thy servant;
for I am afflicted, hear me quickly.

68:19Attend to my soul and redeem it;
because of my enemies, rescue me.

68:20For Thou knowest my reproach, shame and embarrassment;
all those afflicting me are before Thee.

68:21My soul expected reproach and misery;
I waited for someone to grieve with me, but there was none,
for comforters, but found none.

68:22They gave gall for my food,
and for my thirst made me drink sour wine.

68:23Let their table before them become a trap,
a repayment and a stumbling block.

68:24Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see,
and bend their back down continually.

68:25Pour Thine anger upon them;
may the fury of Thine anger seize them.

68:26Let their homestead become deserted;
let no one dwell in their dwellings.

68:27For they persecuted the one Thou didst strike,
and added to the pain of Thy wounded.

68:28Add lawlessness to their lawlessness,
and let them not enter Thy righteousness.

68:29Let them be erased from the book of the living,
and let them not be written with the righteous.

68:30I am poor and in pain,
and the salvation of Thy presence, God, supported me.

68:31I will praise God’s name with a song
and magnify Him in praise,

68:32and it will please God more than a young calf
bringing forth horns and hoofs.

68:33Let the poor see and rejoice;
seek God, and your soul will live,

68:34for the Lord heard the needy
and did not despise His bound ones.

68:35Let the heavens and earth praise Him,
the sea and everything creeping in them.

68:36For God will save Zion,
and Judea’s cities will be built;
they will dwell there and inherit it.

68:37His servants’ offspring will possess it,
and those loving His name will dwell in it.

Psalms 70

Read this chapter on staging

70:1Of David; of the sons of Jonadab and of those first taken captive.
God, in Thee I have hoped;
may I never be disgraced.

70:2In Thy righteousness rescue me and bring me out;
bend Thine ear toward me and save me.

70:3Become for me a defending God
and a fortified place to save me,
for Thou art my firm support and my refuge.

70:4My God, rescue me from a sinner’s hand,
from the hand of one acting lawlessly and unjustly.

70:5For Thou art my endurance, Lord;
the Lord is my hope from my youth.

70:6Upon Thee I was supported from the womb;
from my mother’s belly Thou art the One who shelters me.
My hymn is continually in Thee.

70:7I became like a portent to the many,
and Thou art a mighty helper.

70:8Let my mouth be filled with praise,
so that I may sing of Thy glory,
Thy majesty all day.

70:9Do not cast me away at the time of old age;
when my strength fails, do not forsake me.

70:10For my enemies spoke to me,
and those watching my soul plotted together,

70:11saying, “God has forsaken him!
Pursue him and overtake him,
for there is no rescuer!”

70:12God, do not go far from me;
my God, attend to my help!

70:13Let those slandering my soul be ashamed and fail;
let those seeking evil for me wrap themselves in shame and confusion.

70:14But I will always hope,
and add to all Thy praise.

70:15My mouth will proclaim Thy righteousness,
Thy salvation all day,
for I did not know literary learning.

70:16I will enter in the Lord’s power;
Lord, I will remember Thy righteousness alone.

70:17Thou didst teach me, God, from my youth,
and until now I will announce Thy wonders.

70:18And until old age and advanced years, God, do not forsake me,
until I announce Thine arm to the whole coming generation,
Thy power and Thy righteousness—

70:19God, up to the highest—what great things Thou hast done!
God, who is like Thee?

70:20How many troubles, many and grievous, Thou didst show me!
And turning back, Thou madest me live,
and from the depths of the earth Thou broughtest me up again.

70:21Thou didst increase Thy greatness,
and turning back, didst comfort me,
and from the depths of the earth Thou broughtest me up again.

70:22For I too will acknowledge unto Thee Thy truth with a musical instrument, God;
I will sing unto Thee with a lyre,
Holy One of Israel.

70:23My lips will exult when I sing unto Thee,
and my soul, which Thou didst redeem.

70:24And my tongue too will meditate on Thy righteousness all day,
when those seeking evil for me become ashamed and confounded.

Psalms 71

Read this chapter on staging

71:1For Solomon.
God, give Thy judgment to the king,
and Thy righteousness to the king’s son,

71:2to judge Thy people in righteousness,
and Thy poor in justice.

71:3Let the mountains take up peace for Thy people,
and the hills in righteousness.

71:4He will judge the poor of the people,
and save the children of the needy,
and humble the false accuser,

71:5and he will endure alongside the sun,
and before the moon, through generations of generations.

71:6And he will descend like rain upon a fleece,
and like drops dripping upon the earth.

71:7Righteousness will arise in his days,
and abundant peace until the moon is taken away.

71:8And he will rule from sea to sea,
and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.

71:9Ethiopians will fall before him,
and his enemies will lick dust.

71:10kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts;
kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.

71:11And all kings will bow before him;
all nations will serve him.

71:12For he rescued a poor person from a powerful man’s hand,
and a needy person who had no helper.

71:13He will spare the poor and needy,
and save the souls of the needy.

71:14From interest-taking and injustice he will redeem their souls,
and their name is honored before him.

71:15And he will live, and some of Arabia’s gold will be given to him;
and they will pray concerning him continually,
and bless him all day.

71:16There will be a firm support in the land upon the mountain summits;
his fruit will be raised far above Lebanon,
and they will blossom from the city like the earth’s grass.

71:17Let his name be blessed through the ages;
before the sun his name will endure.
And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him;
all nations will call him blessed.

71:18Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonders!

71:19And blessed be His glorious name for the age and for the age of the age;
and the whole earth will be filled with His glory.
May it be! May it be!

71:20The hymns of David son of Jesse have ended.

Psalms 72

Read this chapter on staging

72:1A psalm of Asaph.
How good God is to Israel,
to those upright in heart!

72:2But my feet were almost shaken;
my steps were nearly poured out.

72:3For I envied the lawless,
beholding sinners’ peace,

72:4for there is no refusal at their death,
and firmness in their scourging.

72:5They are not in human toils,
and they will not be scourged with humans.

72:6Therefore arrogance seized them;
they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.

72:7Their injustice will come out as though from fat;
they passed into a disposition of heart.

72:8They devised and spoke in wickedness;
they spoke injustice against the height.

72:9They set their mouth toward heaven,
and their tongue passed over the earth.

72:10Therefore my people will return here,
and full days will be found for them.

72:11And they said, “How did God know?
And is there knowledge in the Most High?”

72:12Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper;
for the age they took possession of wealth.

72:13And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous
and washed my hands among the innocent;

72:14and I became scourged all day,
and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”

72:15If I were saying, “I will recount it thus,”
behold, I would have broken faith with the generation of Thy sons.

72:16And I undertook to understand this;
it is toil before me,

72:17until I enter God’s sanctuary
and understand their last things.

72:18Nevertheless, because of their deceits Thou didst set things for them;
Thou didst cast them down when they were lifted up.

72:19How they became desolate suddenly!
They failed; they perished through their lawlessness.

72:20Like the dream of someone awakening,
Lord, in Thy city Thou wilt count their image as nothing.

72:21For my heart was set ablaze,
and my kidneys were altered,

72:22and I was counted as nothing and did not understand;
I became beastlike beside Thee.

72:23And I am continually with Thee;
Thou didst grasp my right hand.

72:24In Thy counsel Thou didst guide me,
and with glory Thou didst receive me.

72:25For what is there for me in heaven?
And what did I desire from Thee upon the earth?

72:26My heart and my flesh failed;
the God of my heart and my portion is God for ever.

72:27For behold, those distancing themselves from Thee will perish;
Thou didst destroy everyone who goes whoring away from Thee.

72:28But for me, clinging to God is good,
to set my hope in the Lord,
to proclaim all Thy praises
in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

Psalms 73

Read this chapter on staging

73:1Of understanding. Of Asaph.
Why, God, didst Thou reject to the end?
Why was Thy wrath angry against the sheep of Thy pasture?

73:2Remember Thy congregation, which Thou didst acquire from the beginning;
Thou didst redeem the rod of Thine inheritance,
this Mount Zion, where Thou didst encamp.

73:3Raise Thy hands against their arrogance to the end,
for all the evil the enemy did in Thy holy places.

73:4And those hating Thee boasted within Thy feast;
they set their signs as signs, and did not understand.

73:5As though into the entrance above,

73:6as in a forest of trees, with axes they cut out her doors;
together with axe and stone-cutting tool they tore her down.

73:7They burned Thy sanctuary with fire;
they profaned the tent of Thy name to the ground.

73:8Their kindred said in their hearts together,
“Come, let us burn all God’s feasts from the earth!”

73:9We did not see our signs;
there is no prophet any longer,
and he will know us no longer.

73:10How long, God, will the enemy reproach?
Will the adversary provoke Thy name to the end?

73:11Why dost Thou turn away Thy hand
and Thy right hand from within Thy bosom to the end?

73:12But God is our King before the age;
He worked salvation in the midst of the earth.

73:13Thou didst strengthen the sea by Thy power;
Thou didst crush the dragons’ heads upon the water.

73:14Thou didst crush the dragon’s heads;
Thou gavest him as food to the Ethiopian peoples.

73:15Thou didst break open springs and torrents;
Thou didst dry up rivers of Etham.

73:16Thine is the day, and Thine is the night;
Thou didst fashion light and the sun.

73:17Thou madest all the earth’s boundaries;
summer and spring—Thou didst shape them.

73:18Remember this: an enemy reproached the Lord,
and a foolish people provoked Thy name.

73:19Do not hand over to wild beasts a soul acknowledging Thee;
do not forget Thy needy ones’ souls to the end.

73:20Look upon Thy covenant,
for the darkened ones of the earth were filled with houses of lawlessness.

73:21Let a humbled person not turn back disgraced;
the poor and needy will praise Thy name.

73:22Arise, God, judge Thy case;
remember the reproaches against Thee by a fool all day.

73:23Do not forget Thy suppliants’ voice;
the arrogance of those hating Thee ascended continually toward Thee.

Psalms 74

Read this chapter on staging

74:1For the end. Do not destroy.
A psalm of Asaph, of song.

74:2We will acknowledge Thee, God;
we will acknowledge and call upon Thy name.

74:3I will recount all Thy wonders when I take an appointed time;
I will judge uprightness.

74:4The earth and all who inhabit it melted;
I established its pillars.
Diapsalma.

74:5I said to those acting lawlessly, “Do not act lawlessly,”
and to those sinning, “Do not raise a horn;

74:6do not lift your horn on high;
do not speak injustice against God.”

74:7For neither from the goings-out nor from the settings,
nor from desert mountains,

74:8for God is judge:
He humbles this one and raises that one.

74:9For in the Lord’s hand is a cup
of unmixed wine, full of mixture;
and He tilted from this into that,
but its dregs were not emptied out;
all the earth’s sinners will drink.

74:10But I will exult for ever;
I will sing to the God of Jacob.

74:11And I will break together all sinners’ horns;
and the righteous person’s horns will be raised.

Diapsalma.

Psalms 76

Read this chapter on staging

76:1For the end, concerning Jeduthun.
Of Asaph. A psalm.

76:2With my voice I cried to the Lord,
with my voice to God, and He attended to me.

76:3In the day of my affliction I sought God,
with my hands at night before Him, and I was not deceived;
my soul refused to be comforted.

76:4I remembered God and was glad;
I spoke at length, and my spirit lost heart.
Diapsalma.

76:5My eyes anticipated the watches;
I was troubled and did not speak.

76:6I considered ancient days,
and remembered everlasting years and meditated.

76:7At night I spoke at length with my heart,
and my spirit kept searching.

76:8“Will the Lord reject for the ages,
and not again take pleasure?

76:9Or will He cut off His mercy to the end,
from generation to generation?

76:10Or will God forget to show pity,
or hold His compassions shut in His wrath?”
Diapsalma.

76:11And I said, “Now I have begun;
this is the change of the Most High’s right hand.”

76:12I remembered the Lord’s works,
for I will remember Thy wonders from the beginning,

76:13and meditate on all Thy works,
and speak at length about Thy practices.

76:14God, Thy way is in the Holy One;
what god is great like our God?

76:15Thou art the God who does wonders;
Thou madest Thy power known among the peoples.

76:16With Thine arm Thou didst redeem Thy people,
the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
Diapsalma.

76:17The waters saw Thee, God;
the waters saw Thee and feared,
and the depths were troubled—a multitude of sounding waters.

76:18The clouds gave voice,
for Thine arrows too pass through.

76:19Thy thunder’s voice was in the wheel;
Thy flashes of lightning shone upon the inhabited world;
the earth shook and became trembling.

76:20Thy way is in the sea,
and Thy paths in many waters,
and Thy tracks will not be known.

76:21Thou didst guide Thy people like sheep
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

Psalms 77

Read this chapter on staging

77:1Of understanding. Of Asaph.
Attend, my people, to my law;
bend your ear to the words of my mouth.

77:2I will open my mouth in parables;
I will utter riddles from the beginning,

77:3whatever we heard and knew,
and our fathers recounted to us,

77:4it was not hidden from their children for another generation,
as we announce the Lord’s praises,
His mighty acts and the wonders He did.

77:5And He raised a testimony in Jacob
and set a law in Israel,
whatever He commanded our fathers
to make known to their sons,

77:6so that another generation might know,
sons who will be born;
and they will rise and announce it to their sons,

77:7so that they may set their hope upon God
and not forget God’s works,
and seek out His commandments,

77:8so that they may not become like their fathers,
a crooked and embittering generation,
a generation that did not direct its heart,
whose spirit was not faithful with God.

77:9The sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting bows,
turned back on the day of war.

77:10They did not keep God’s covenant
and were unwilling to walk in His law,

77:11and forgot His benefits
and the wonders He showed them,

77:12the wonders He did before their fathers,
in Egypt’s land, in the plain of Tanis.

77:13He tore the sea apart and led them through;
He stood the waters like a skin-bag,

77:14and guided them with a cloud by day,
and all night with the light of fire.

77:15He split a rock in the wilderness
and gave them drink as in a great deep,

77:16and brought water out of a rock
and made waters descend like rivers.

77:17And they continued still to sin against Him;
they embittered the Most High in a waterless place,

77:18and put God to the test in their hearts,
asking food for their souls,

77:19and spoke against God and said,
“Surely God cannot prepare a table in a wilderness?

77:20Since He struck a rock and waters flowed,
and torrents were flooded,
surely He cannot also give bread
or prepare a table for His people?”

77:21Therefore the Lord heard and delayed;
and fire was kindled in Jacob,
and wrath rose against Israel,

77:22because they did not believe in God
nor hope in His salvation.

77:23And He commanded the clouds above
and opened heaven’s doors,

77:24and rained manna for them to eat,
and gave them heaven’s bread.

77:25A man ate angels’ bread;
He sent them food supplies to fullness.

77:26He moved the south wind from heaven,
and brought the southwest wind by His power,

77:27and rained flesh upon them like dust,
and winged birds like the sands of seas,

77:28and they fell within their camp,
around their tents,

77:29and they ate and were filled exceedingly,
and He brought them their desire.

77:30They were not deprived of their desire.
While their food was still in their mouth,

77:31then God’s wrath rose against them,
and He killed among their fat ones,
and entangled Israel’s chosen men.

77:32In all these things they sinned still
and did not believe in His wonders,

77:33and their days failed in futility,
and their years with haste.

77:34Whenever He killed them, they sought Him;
and they returned and rose early toward God,

77:35and remembered that God is their helper,
and God Most High is their redeemer.

77:36And they deceived Him with their mouth,
and lied to Him with their tongue,

77:37but their heart was not upright with Him,
nor were they faithful in His covenant.

77:38But He is compassionate;
He will make atonement for their sins and not destroy,
and will turn back His wrath again and again,
and will not kindle all His anger.

77:39And He remembered that they are flesh,
a spirit going away and not returning.

77:40How often they embittered Him in the wilderness
and angered Him in a waterless land!

77:41And they turned again and tested God,
and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

77:42They did not remember His hand,
the day He redeemed them from an oppressor’s hand,

77:43how He set His signs in Egypt
and His portents in the plain of Tanis,

77:44and turned their rivers into blood,
and their rain-waters, so that they might not drink.

77:45He sent a dog-fly among them, and it devoured them,
and a frog, and it destroyed them.

77:46And He gave their fruit to mildew,
and their labors to the locust.

77:47He killed their vine with hail,
and their sycamores with frost.

77:48And He handed their cattle over to hail,
and their possessions to fire.

77:49He sent upon them the anger of His wrath,
wrath, anger and affliction,
a mission through evil angels.

77:50He made a road for His wrath;
He did not spare their souls from death,
and confined their cattle to death,

77:51and struck every firstborn in Egypt,
the firstfruits of their labors in Ham’s tents.

77:52And He led His people away like sheep,
and brought them up like a flock in the wilderness,

77:53and guided them in hope, and they did not grow cowardly;
and the sea covered their enemies.

77:54And He brought them into the boundary of His sanctuary,
this mountain which His right hand acquired,

77:55and expelled nations from before them,
and assigned them by a cord of inheritance,
and settled Israel’s tribes in their tents.

77:56And they tested and embittered God Most High,
and did not keep His testimonies,

77:57and turned back and broke faith just like their fathers,
and changed into a crooked bow,

77:58and angered Him with their hills,
and provoked Him to jealousy with their carvings.

77:59God heard and disregarded,
and counted Israel as utterly nothing,

77:60and rejected Shiloh’s tent,
His dwelling, where He encamped among humans.

77:61And He handed their strength over to captivity,
and their beauty into an enemy’s hands,

77:62and confined His people to the sword,
and disregarded His inheritance.

77:63Fire devoured their young men,
and their virgins were not mourned.

77:64Their priests fell by the sword,
and their widows will not be wept for.

77:65And the Lord awoke like one sleeping,
like a powerful man heavy with wine,

77:66and struck His enemies backward;
He gave them everlasting reproach.

77:67And He rejected Joseph’s dwelling,
and did not choose Ephraim’s tribe.

77:68And He chose Judah’s tribe,
Mount Zion, which He loved,

77:69and built His sanctuary like that of one-horned beasts;
in the earth He founded it for ever.

77:70And He chose David His servant,
and took him up from the flocks of sheep;

77:71from behind the ewes giving birth He took him,
to shepherd Jacob His people
and Israel His inheritance.

77:72And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence,
and guided them with his hands’ understanding.

Current Bespoke editorial notes

The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Human address uses your; light of fire, great deep and singular man give natural English. Then connects the wrath clause with while in 30; turning back wrath again and again expresses repeated action. All 72 units, parables/riddles, singular frog/dog-fly, angels’ bread, evil angels, south/southwest winds, delayed, one-horned beasts, fat ones and past/future distinctions retained.

Psalms 78

78:1A psalm for Asaph.
God, nations entered Thine inheritance;
they defiled Thy holy temple;
they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.

78:2They made the dead bodies of Thy servants
food for the birds of heaven,
the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.

78:3They poured out their blood like water
around Jerusalem,
and there was no one to bury them.

78:4We became a reproach to our neighbors,
sneering and ridicule to those around us.

78:5How long, Lord? Wilt Thou be angry to the end?
Will Thy jealousy blaze like fire?

78:6Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee,
and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,

78:7for they devoured Jacob
and made his place desolate.

78:8Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness;
let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first,
for we became very poor.

78:9Help us, God our Savior.
For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us,
and be propitious toward our sins
for Thy name’s sake,

78:10lest the nations say, “Where is their God?”
And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants
be known among the nations before our eyes.

78:11Let the groaning of those in bonds enter before Thee;
according to the greatness of Thine arm,
preserve the sons of those put to death.

78:12Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom
their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.

78:13But we, Thy people and the sheep of Thy pasture,
will give Thee thanks for ever;
from generation to generation we will proclaim Thy praise.

79:1For the end; concerning those who will be changed.
A testimony for Asaph; a psalm concerning the Assyrian.

79:2Thou who shepherdest Israel, pay attention,

79:3Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh,

and come to save us.

79:4God, turn us back;
make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.

79:5Lord, God of powers,

make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.
Diapsalma.

79:9Thou didst transplant a vine from Egypt;

79:10Thou madest a road before her
and didst plant her roots,
and the land was filled.

79:11Her shadow covered mountains,
and her climbing branches covered God’s cedars.

79:12She stretched her branches as far as the sea,
and her offshoots as far as the River.

79:13Why didst Thou tear down her fence,
so that all who pass along the road harvest her?

79:14A pig from the woodland ravaged her,
and a solitary wild beast grazed her down.

79:15God of powers, turn back now;
look from heaven and see,
and visit this vine,

79:16and restore her whom Thy right hand planted,
and upon the son of man whom Thou didst strengthen for Thyself.

at the rebuke of Thy face they will perish.

79:18Let Thy hand come upon the man of Thy right hand
and upon the son of man whom Thou didst strengthen for Thyself.

79:19And we shall certainly not depart from Thee;

79:20Lord, God of powers, turn us back;
make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.

Psalms 80

80:1For the end; concerning the winepresses. A psalm for Asaph.

80:2Exult in God our helper;
raise a shout to the God of Jacob.

80:3Take up a psalm and sound the tambourine,
a delightful psaltery together with a lyre.

80:4Sound the trumpet at the new moon,
on the conspicuous day of our feast.

80:5For it is an ordinance for Israel
and a judgment of the God of Jacob.

80:6He established it as a testimony in Joseph,
when he went out from the land of Egypt;
a language he did not know, he heard.

80:7He removed his back from burdens;
his hands served at the basket.

80:8In affliction you called on Me, and I delivered you;

Diapsalma.

80:9Hear, My people, and I solemnly testify to you;
Israel, if you listen to Me,

80:10There shall be no new god among you,
nor shall you bow down to a foreign god.

80:11For I am the Lord your God,
who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

80:12And My people did not listen to My voice,
and Israel did not pay attention to Me.

80:13So I sent them away according to the practices of their hearts;
they will walk in their practices.

80:14If My people had listened to Me,
if Israel had walked in My ways,

80:15in no time I would have humbled their enemies
and laid My hand upon those who afflict them.

80:16The Lord’s enemies lied to Him,
and their appointed time will be for ever.

and with honey from rock He satisfied them.

82:1A song of a psalm for Asaph.

82:2God, who will be likened unto Thee?

84:2Thou tookest pleasure in Thy land, Lord;

Diapsalma.

and our land will give its fruit.

85:1A prayer for David.

85:2Guard my soul, for I am holy;

85:3Have mercy on me, Lord,

Psalms 87

Read this chapter on staging

87:1A song of a psalm for the sons of Korah.
For the end; concerning Maeleth, for answering.
Of understanding; of Heman the Israelite.

87:2Lord, God of my salvation,
by day I cried out, and by night before Thee.

87:3Let my prayer enter before Thee;
incline Thine ear to my petition, Lord.

87:4For my soul was filled with evils,
and my life drew near Hades.

87:5I was counted with those descending into a pit;
I became like a person without help,
free among the dead,

87:6like wounded people cast down, sleeping in a grave,
whom Thou didst remember no more,
and who were thrust away from Thy hand.

87:7They put me in the lowest pit,
in dark places and in death’s shadow.

87:8Thy fury rested firmly upon me,
and Thou broughtest all Thy surges upon me.
Diapsalma.

87:9Thou didst remove my acquaintances far from me;
they made me an abomination to themselves.
I was handed over and did not go out.

87:10My eyes grew weak from poverty.
I cried unto Thee, Lord, all day;
I spread my hands toward Thee:

87:11Surely Thou wilt not work wonders for the dead?
Or will physicians raise them, and will they give Thee thanks?

87:12Surely no one will recount Thy mercy in a grave
and Thy truth in destruction?

87:13Surely Thy wonders will not be known in darkness,
or Thy righteousness in a forgotten land?

87:14And I cried unto Thee, Lord,
and in the morning my prayer will reach Thee first.

87:15Why, Lord, dost Thou thrust away my soul
and turn Thy face away from me?

87:16I am poor and in toils from my youth;
but after being raised up, I was humbled and left helpless.

87:17Thy wraths passed over me,
and Thy threats utterly troubled me;

87:18they encircled me like water all day;
together they closed around me.

87:19Thou didst remove friend and neighbor far from me,
and my acquaintances because of misery.

Psalms 88

Read this chapter on staging

88:1Of understanding; of Ethan the Israelite.

88:2I will sing of Thy mercies, Lord, for ever;

88:3for Thou saidst, “Mercy will be built for ever;

88:4“I made a covenant with My chosen ones;

88:5‘I will prepare your seed for ever

Diapsalma.

88:6The heavens will acknowledge Thy wonders, Lord,
and Thy truth in an assembly of holy ones.

88:7For who in clouds will be equaled to the Lord,
and who among sons of God will be likened to the Lord?

88:8God is glorified in the council of holy ones,
great and fearsome above all around Him.

88:9Lord, God of powers, who is like Thee?
Thou art mighty, Lord, and Thy truth surrounds Thee.

88:10Thou rulest the sea’s might,
and Thou quietest the surge of its waves.

88:11Thou didst humble a proud one like a wounded man,
and with the arm of Thy power Thou didst scatter Thine enemies.

88:12The heavens are Thine, and the earth is Thine;
the inhabited world and its fullness—Thou didst found them.

88:13The north and seas—Thou didst create them;
Tabor and Hermon will exult in Thy name.

88:14Thine is the arm with dominion;
let Thy hand be strengthened; let Thy right hand be raised.

88:15Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of Thy throne;
mercy and truth will go ahead before Thy face.

88:16Blessed are the people who know the cry of triumph;
Lord, they will walk in the light of Thy face,

88:17and in Thy name they will exult all day,
and in Thy righteousness they will be raised up.

88:18For Thou art the boast of their power,
and by Thy favor our horn will be raised.

88:19For support belongs to the Lord,
and to the Holy One of Israel, our King.

88:20Then Thou spakest in a vision to Thy holy ones and saidst:
“I placed help upon a powerful man;
I raised a chosen one from My people.

88:21I found David My servant;
with My holy oil I anointed him,

88:22for My hand will support him,
and My arm will strengthen him.

88:23An enemy will not gain by him,
and a son of lawlessness will not go on to harm him.

88:24I will cut down his enemies before him
and put those who hate him to flight.

88:25My truth and My mercy will be with him,
and in My name his horn will be raised.

88:26I will set his hand in the sea
and his right hand in rivers.

88:27He will call on Me, ‘Thou art my Father,
my God and the supporter of my salvation.’

88:28And I will make him firstborn,
high among the kings of the earth.

88:29For ever I will keep My mercy for him,
and My covenant is faithful to him.

88:30I will establish his seed for an age of an age
and his throne like the days of heaven.

88:31If his sons abandon My law
and do not walk in My judgments,

88:32if they profane My ordinances
and do not keep My commandments,

88:33I will visit their lawless acts with a rod
and their sins with scourges;

88:34but I shall certainly not scatter My mercy away from him,
nor act unjustly in My truth,

88:35nor shall I profane My covenant,
and what goes out through My lips I shall certainly not set aside.

88:36Once I swore by My holiness:
I will not lie to David.

88:37His seed will remain for ever,
and his throne will be like the sun before Me,

88:38and like the moon, established for ever;
and the witness in heaven is faithful.”
Diapsalma.

88:39But Thou didst reject and treat as nothing;
Thou didst put off Thine anointed.

88:40Thou didst overturn Thy servant’s covenant;
Thou didst profane his consecrated thing to the ground.

88:41Thou didst tear down all his fences;
Thou madest his fortifications cowardice.

88:42All who travel the road plundered him;
he became a reproach to his neighbors.

88:43Thou didst raise the right hand of his enemies;
Thou didst gladden all his enemies.

88:44Thou didst turn back the help of his sword
and didst not support him in war.

88:45Thou didst remove him from purification;
Thou didst dash his throne down to the ground.

88:46Thou didst shorten the days of his time;
Thou didst pour shame over him.
Diapsalma.

88:47How long, Lord? Wilt Thou turn away to the end?
Will Thy wrath blaze like fire?

88:48Remember what my existence is;
for surely Thou didst not create all the sons of men in vain?

88:49Who is the person who will live and not see death,
who will deliver his soul from the hand of Hades?
Diapsalma.

88:50Where are Thine ancient mercies, Lord,
which Thou didst swear to David in Thy truth?

88:51Remember, Lord, the reproach of Thy servants,
which I bore in my bosom from many nations,

88:52with which Thine enemies reproached, Lord,
with which they reproached the exchange of Thine anointed.

88:53Blessed be the Lord for ever.
May it be; may it be.

Psalms 89

Read this chapter on staging

89:1A prayer of Moses, the man of God.
Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.

89:2Before the mountains came to be
and the earth and inhabited world were formed,
from age to age Thou art.

89:3Do not turn a man toward humiliation;
and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.

89:4For a thousand years in Thine eyes
are like yesterday, which passed,
and a watch in the night.

89:5Their things counted as nothing will be years.
In the morning, like green grass, may it pass away;

89:6in the morning may it blossom and pass away;
in the evening may it fall, grow hard and dry up.

89:7For we failed in Thine anger
and were troubled in Thy wrath.

89:8Thou didst set our lawless deeds before Thee;
our age is in the light of Thy face.

89:9For all our days failed,
and in Thine anger we failed;
I pondered our years like a spider.

89:10The days of our years—in them are seventy years,
or, with strength, eighty years;
the greater part of them is toil and pain,
for gentleness came upon us, and we shall be disciplined.

89:11Who knows the might of Thine anger,
and Thy wrath from the fear of Thee?

89:12So make known how to number Thy right hand,
and those bound in heart in wisdom.

89:13Return, Lord—how long?
Be moved concerning Thy servants.

89:14We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy,
and we exulted and rejoiced all our days.

89:15We were glad in return for the days Thou didst humble us,
the years when we saw evils.

89:16Look upon Thy servants and Thy works,
and guide their children.

89:17Let the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us,
and direct the works of our hands for us.

Psalms 90

Read this chapter on staging

90:1A praise of a song, of David.
The one dwelling in the help of the Most High
will lodge in the shelter of the God of heaven.

90:2He will say to the Lord, Thou art my Helper and my refuge,
my God; I will hope in Him.

90:3For He will rescue me from the hunters’ trap
and from a disturbing word.

90:4With His shoulders He will overshadow you,
and under His wings you will hope;
His truth will surround you with a weapon.

90:5You will not fear terror by night,
the missile flying by day,

90:6the thing passing through darkness,
the calamity and the demon of noon.

90:7A thousand will fall at your side
and ten thousand at your right hand,
but it will not come near you.

90:8You will only observe with your eyes
and see the repayment of sinners.

90:9For Thou, Lord, art my hope.
You have made the Most High your refuge.

90:10Evils will not approach you,
and a scourge will not come near your dwelling.

90:11For He will command His angels concerning you,
to guard you in all your ways.

90:12On their hands they will lift you,
lest you strike your foot against a stone.

90:13You will step on an asp and a basilisk,
and trample a lion and a dragon.

90:14Because he hoped in Me, I will rescue him;
I will shelter him, because he knew My name.

90:15He will call upon Me, and I will hear him;
I am with him in affliction,
and I will take him out and glorify him.

90:16With length of days I will fill him
and show him My salvation.

Saints English wording notes

Psalms 90:1 · help

Sense. Aid belonging to God in the dwelling image.

Keep help and the following shelter as two related images. Retain God of heaven in the second clause; a familiar divine title in another witness cannot replace the stated designation.

Historical comparison. KJV has secret place and Almighty. Brenton follows help and God of heaven; DRC has aid and God of Jacob. These are more than stylistic synonyms.

Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek chapter · Lexical record carried forward from the Saints Biblical Lexicon, Wisdom review, 26 September 2026. Independent linguistic review remains outstanding.

Psalms 90:9 · change of addressee

The first clause addresses the Lord; the second speaks of making the Most High a refuge. Both addresses are singular. The second Thou is capitalized only because it begins a sentence; thy remains lower case. Checked in the publisher running text on 30 September 2026.

Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek chapter · Editorial grammar note; no complete critical-apparatus review is claimed.

Help/shelter/God of heaven, shoulders, me in 3, weapon, demon, basilisk and all ways retained. Historical note describing the former sentence-initial Thou in 9 remains unchanged and is superseded by the new policy note.

Psalms 93

Read this chapter on staging

93:1A psalm of David, for the fourth day of the week.
The God of vengeance is the Lord;
the God of vengeance spoke openly.

93:2Be exalted, Judge of the earth;
give repayment to the arrogant.

93:3How long, Lord, will sinners—
how long will sinners boast,

93:4utter and speak injustice—
will all who work lawlessness speak?

93:5They humbled Thy people, Lord,
and mistreated Thine inheritance.

93:6They killed the widow and newcomer
and murdered orphans.

93:7They said, The Lord will not see,
nor will the God of Jacob understand.

93:8Understand now, you senseless among the people;
and you fools, become wise at last.

93:9Does the One who planted the ear not hear,
or the One who formed the eye not perceive?

93:10Will the One who disciplines nations not rebuke—
the One who teaches humankind knowledge?

93:11The Lord knows human reasonings,
that they are futile.

93:12Happy the person Thou disciplinest, Lord,
whom Thou teachest from Thy law,

93:13to soothe him from evil days,
until a pit is dug for the sinner.

93:14For the Lord will not reject His people,
nor abandon His inheritance,

93:15until righteousness returns to judgment,
and all the upright in heart cling to it. Diapsalma.

93:16Who will rise for me against evildoers,
or who will stand beside me against workers of lawlessness?

93:17Had the Lord not helped me,
my soul would almost have sojourned in Hades.

93:18If I said, My foot has been shaken,
Thy mercy, Lord, helps me.

93:19Lord, amid the multitude of pains in my heart,
Thy consolations loved my soul.

93:20Will a throne of lawlessness join Thee,
one that shapes toil by command?

93:21They will hunt a righteous person’s soul
and condemn innocent blood.

Psalms 101

Read this chapter on staging

101:1A prayer of a poor person when he becomes despondent and pours out his petition before the Lord.

101:2Hear my prayer, Lord,
and let my cry come unto Thee.

101:3Do not turn Thy face away from me.
On whatever day I am afflicted, incline Thine ear to me;
on whatever day I call upon Thee, hear me quickly.

101:4For my days vanished like smoke,
and my bones were scorched like kindling.

101:5My heart was struck like grass and dried up,
for I forgot to eat my bread.

101:6From the sound of my groaning,
my bone clung to my flesh.

101:7I became like a wilderness pelican;
I became like a night raven on a house site.

101:8I stayed awake and became
like a little bird alone on a roof.

101:9All day my enemies reproached me,
and those praising me swore against me.

101:10For I ate ashes like bread
and mixed my drink with weeping,

101:11because of Thine anger and wrath,
for after lifting me up Thou didst dash me down.

101:12My days bent like a shadow,
and I dried up like grass.

101:13But Thou, Lord, remainest for ever,
and Thy memorial is from generation to generation.

101:14Thou wilt arise and have compassion on Zion,
for it is time to have compassion on her; the time has come.

101:15For Thy servants took pleasure in her stones
and will have compassion on her dust.

101:16Nations will fear the Lord’s name,
and all the kings of the earth Thy glory,

101:17for the Lord will build Zion
and will appear in His glory.

101:18He looked upon the prayer of the lowly
and did not treat their petition as nothing.

101:19Let this be written for another generation,
and the people being created will praise the Lord,

101:20for He leaned out from His holy height;
the Lord looked from heaven upon the earth,

101:21to hear the groaning of those in bonds,
to release the sons of those put to death,

101:22to announce the Lord’s name in Zion
and His praise in Jerusalem,

101:23when peoples are gathered together,
and kingdoms, to serve the Lord.

101:24He answered him in the way of his strength:
Tell me the fewness of my days.

101:25Do not take me up at the halfway point of my days;
Thy years extend through a generation of generations.

101:26At the beginning Thou, Lord, didst found the earth,
and the heavens are works of Thy hands.

101:27They will perish, but Thou wilt remain;
all will grow old like a garment.
Like a cloak Thou wilt change them, and they will be changed.

101:28But Thou art the same,
and Thy years will not fail.

101:29The children of Thy servants will make their dwelling,
and their offspring will be established for ever.

who crowns you with mercy and compassions;

102:5who fills your desire with good things;
your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.

102:6The Lord does deeds of mercy
and judgment for all who are wronged.

His wishes to the sons of Israel.

102:8The Lord is compassionate and merciful,
patient and abundant in mercy.

102:9He will not be angry to the end,
nor maintain wrath for ever.

102:10He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,

102:11for according to heaven’s height above the earth,
the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him.

102:12As far as the east is distant from the west,
He removed our lawless deeds from us.

102:13As a father has compassion on children,
the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,

102:14for He knew our formation.
Remember that we are dust.

102:15A man—his days are like grass;
like a flower of the field, so he will flower,

102:16for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist,
and he will no longer recognize his place.

and His righteousness toward children’s children,

102:18to those who keep His covenant
and remember His commandments to do them.

102:19The Lord prepared His throne in heaven,
and His kingdom has dominion over all.

102:20Bless the Lord, all His angels,
mighty in strength, doing His word,
so as to hear the voice of His words.

102:21Bless the Lord, all His powers,
His ministers who do His will.

102:22Bless the Lord, all His works,
in every place of His dominion.
Bless the Lord, my soul.

Saints English wording notes

Psalms 102:4 · corruption

Sense. Decay or destruction threatening life in the redemption statement.

Keep corruption with decay or destruction as its contextual explanation. The verse concerns life rescued from ruin; it does not make this occurrence a direct statement about bribery or moral corruption.

Historical comparison. KJV and DRC use destruction, while Saints and Brenton use corruption. Preserve mercy and compassion as the following coordinated gifts.

Psalms 103

Read this chapter on staging

103:1Of David.
Bless the Lord, my soul.
Lord my God, Thou hast become very great;
Thou hast clothed Thyself in praise and dignity,

103:2wrapping Thyself in light like a garment,
stretching out heaven like a hide curtain;

103:3He roofs His upper chambers in waters,
makes clouds His means of ascent,
and walks on the wings of winds.

103:4He makes His angels winds,
and His ministers a burning fire.

103:5He founded the earth on its stability;
it will not be tilted for an age of ages.

103:6The deep is His covering like a garment;
waters will stand upon the mountains.

103:7At Thy rebuke they will flee;
at the voice of Thy thunder they will become afraid.

103:8Mountains rise and plains descend
to the place Thou didst found for them.

103:9Thou didst set a boundary they will not pass,
nor will they return to cover the earth.

103:10He sends springs into the ravines;
waters will pass between the mountains.

103:11They give drink to all the beasts of the field;
wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.

103:12Upon them the birds of heaven will nest;
from among the rocks they will give voice.

103:13He waters mountains from His upper chambers;
the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.

103:14He makes grass spring up for livestock
and green plants for the service of humans,
to bring bread out of the earth;

103:15and wine gladdens the human heart,
to brighten the face with oil,
and bread makes the human heart firm.

103:16The trees of the plain will be filled,
the cedars of Lebanon that He planted;

103:17there sparrows will nest;
the heron’s house leads them.

103:18The high mountains are for deer;
a rock is a refuge for rock rabbits.

103:19He made the moon for seasons;
the sun knew its setting.

103:20Thou didst set darkness, and night came to be;
in it all the beasts of the forest will pass,

103:21young lions roaring to seize prey
and to seek food for themselves from God.

103:22The sun rose, and they gathered,
and they will lie down in their enclosures.

103:23A man will go out to his work
and to his labor until evening.

103:24How great Thy works have become, Lord!
Thou madest all things in wisdom;
the earth was filled with Thy possession.

103:25Here is the sea, great and spacious;
there are creeping things without number,
living creatures small with great.

103:26There ships pass,
and this dragon, which Thou didst form to play with it.

103:27All wait for Thee
to give them food at the right time.

103:28When Thou givest to them, they will gather;
when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.

103:29When Thou turnest Thy face away, they will be troubled.
Thou wilt take back their breath, and they will fail
and return to their dust.

103:30Thou wilt send Thy Spirit, and they will be created,
and Thou wilt renew the face of the earth.

103:31Let the Lord’s glory be for ever;
the Lord will rejoice in His works.

103:32He looks upon the earth and makes it tremble;
He touches the mountains, and they smoke.

103:33I will sing to the Lord in my life;
I will make music to my God as long as I exist.

103:34May my meditation be sweet to Him;
as for me, I will rejoice in the Lord.

103:35May sinners vanish from the earth,
and lawless people, so that they no longer exist.
Bless the Lord, my soul.

and killed their fish.

104:30Their land teemed with frogs
in the chambers of their kings.

104:31He spoke, and dog-flies came,
and gnats throughout all their borders.

104:32He made their rains hail,
consuming fire in their land,

104:33and struck their vines and fig trees
and shattered every tree of their border.

104:34He spoke, and locusts came,
and locust larvae without number,

104:35and devoured all the grass in their land
and devoured the fruit of their land.

104:36He struck every firstborn in their land,
the firstfruits of all their toil,

104:37and brought them out with silver and gold,
and none among their tribes was weak.

104:38Egypt rejoiced at their departure,
for fear of them had fallen upon them.

104:39He spread a cloud as a shelter for them
and fire to light the night for them.

104:40They asked, and quail came,
and He filled them with bread from heaven.

104:41He split a rock, and waters flowed;
rivers traveled through waterless places.

104:42For He remembered His holy word
to Abraham His servant,

104:43and brought His people out in exultation
and His chosen ones in gladness.

104:44He gave them countries of nations,
and they inherited the toils of peoples,

104:45so that they might keep His ordinances
and diligently seek His law.

Saints English wording notes

Psalms 104:11 · singular and plural

The source changes from singular soi to plural hymōn: To thee … your inheritance. The English retains both numbers within the same verse. Checked in the publisher running text on 30 September 2026.

In 11, To you is singular in Greek (soi), but your inheritance is plural (hymon); this number shift is explained here under the newer policy, while the historical thee/your note is preserved. Psalms 105

Read this chapter on staging

105:1Hallelujah.
Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good;
His mercy is for ever.

105:2Who will speak the Lord’s mighty deeds,
make all His praises heard?

105:3Blessed are those who keep judgment
and do righteousness at every time.

105:4Remember us, Lord, with the favor of Thy people;
visit us with Thy salvation,

105:5that we may see the goodness of Thy chosen ones,
rejoice in the gladness of Thy nation,
and be praised with Thine inheritance.

105:6We sinned with our fathers;
we acted lawlessly and unjustly.

105:7Our fathers in Egypt did not understand Thy wonders;
they did not remember the abundance of Thy mercy
and provoked Thee while going up in the Red Sea.

105:8He saved them for His name’s sake,
to make His might known.

105:9He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up;
He guided them in the deep as in a wilderness.

105:10He saved them from the hand of those hating them
and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

105:11Water covered those afflicting them;
not one of them was left.

105:12They believed His words
and sang His praise.

105:13They hurried and forgot His works;
they did not wait for His counsel.

105:14They desired a desire in the wilderness
and tested God in a waterless place.

105:15He gave them their request
and sent fullness into their souls.

105:16They angered Moses in the camp,
and Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.

105:17The earth was opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered Abiram’s assembly.

105:18Fire was kindled in their assembly;
a flame burned up sinners.

105:19They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a carved image.

105:20They exchanged their glory
for the likeness of a calf that eats grass.

105:21They forgot the God who saved them,
who did great things in Egypt,

105:22wonders in the land of Ham,
fearful things at the Red Sea.

105:23He said He would destroy them,
had not Moses His chosen one stood in the breach before Him,
to turn His anger away so He would not destroy.

105:24They treated the desirable land as nothing;
they did not believe His word.

105:25They grumbled in their dwellings;
they did not hear the Lord’s voice.

105:26He lifted His hand to them,
to cast them down in the wilderness,

105:27and to cast their offspring down among the nations,
and scatter them in the countries.

105:28They were initiated to Baal-peor
and ate sacrifices of the dead.

105:29They provoked Him with their practices,
and the falling multiplied among them.

105:30Phinehas stood and made atonement,
and the breaking ceased.

105:31It was reckoned to him as righteousness,
from generation to generation for ever.

105:32They angered Him at the water of contradiction,
and Moses suffered harm because of them,

105:33for they embittered his spirit,
and he issued a command with his lips.

105:34They did not destroy the nations
of which the Lord had spoken to them,

105:35and mixed with the nations
and learned their works.

105:36They served their carved images,
and it became a stumbling block to them.

105:37They sacrificed their sons
and their daughters to demons,

105:38and shed innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters whom they sacrificed to Canaan’s carved images;
the land was murdered with blood,

105:39and was defiled by their works,
and they prostituted themselves through their practices.

105:40The Lord was wrathfully angry against His people
and abhorred His inheritance.

105:41He handed them over into nations’ hands,
and those hating them became their masters.

105:42Their enemies afflicted them,
and they were humbled beneath their hands.

105:43Many times He rescued them,
but they provoked Him in their counsel
and were humbled in their lawless deeds.

105:44He saw when they were afflicted,
when He heard their petition.

105:45He remembered His covenant
and changed His purpose according to His abundant mercy,

105:46and granted them compassions
before all who had taken them captive.

105:47Save us, Lord our God,
and gather us together from the nations,
to give thanks to Thy holy name
and boast in Thy praise.

105:48Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from eternity to eternity.
All the people will say, May it be, may it be.

108:1For the end. Of David. A psalm.
God, do not pass over my praise in silence,

108:2for a sinner’s mouth and a deceitful person’s mouth were opened against me;
they spoke against me with a deceitful tongue,

108:3and surrounded me with words of hatred

108:4Instead of loving me, they were slandering me,

108:5They set evils against me in exchange for good things
and hatred in exchange for my love.

108:6Appoint a sinner over him,
and let a slanderer stand at his right hand.

108:7When he is judged, may he come out condemned,
and let his prayer become sin.

108:8Let his days become few,
and may another take his oversight.

108:9Let his sons become orphans
and his wife a widow.

108:10Let his sons be shaken and migrate, and let them beg;
let them be cast out from their house sites.

108:11Let a lender search out everything he possesses;
let strangers plunder his toils.

108:12Let no helper exist for him,
nor anyone compassionate toward his orphans.

108:13Let his children be destroyed;
in one generation let his name be erased.

108:14May his fathers’ lawlessness be remembered before the Lord,
and may his mother’s sin not be erased.

108:15Let them be before the Lord continually,
and may their memorial be destroyed from the earth,

108:16because he did not remember to show mercy
and pursued a poor and needy person
and one pierced in heart, to put him to death.

108:17He loved a curse, and it will come to him;
he did not desire blessing, and it will be far from him.

108:18He clothed himself in a curse like a garment;
it entered his innards like water
and his bones like oil.

108:19Let it become for him like a garment he puts around himself
and like a belt he continually fastens.

108:20This is the work of those slandering me, from the Lord,
and of those speaking evil against my soul.

108:21But Thou, Lord, Lord, show mercy with me for Thy name’s sake,
for Thy mercy is good.

108:22Rescue me, for I am poor and needy,
and my heart is troubled within me.

108:23Like a shadow as it declines, I was taken away;
I was shaken off like locusts.

108:24My knees grew weak from fasting,
and my flesh was altered because of oil.

108:25I became a reproach to them;
they saw me and shook their heads.

108:26Help me, Lord my God;
save me according to Thy mercy,

108:27and let them know that this is Thy hand
and that Thou, Lord, hast done it.

108:28They will curse, but Thou wilt bless;
let those rising against me be ashamed,
but Thy servant will rejoice.

108:29Let those slandering me wear humiliation
and wrap themselves in their shame like a double cloak.

108:30I will greatly thank the Lord with my mouth
and praise Him among many,

108:31for He stood at a poor person’s right hand,
to save from those pursuing my soul.

Saints English wording notes

Psalms 109:4 · repent

Sense. Will not reconsider or go back on the declared oath.

Use change His purpose in the oath context. Traditional will not repent remains possible with a note explaining reconsideration; the English word must not suggest confession of divine wrongdoing.

Historical comparison. KJV, Brenton, and DRC use repent. The Saints wording clarifies the oath's continuing force. Preserve the separately stated priesthood and order of Melchizedek.

Royal address uses you/your, including God’s priesthood declaration. My lord remains lowercase, and capitalization does not decide identity. Womb, morning star, begot, Melchizedek, unchanged purpose and final lowercase he retained. Specialist review must address speakers in 3–7 and the inherited supplied field in 6, which is not an explicit Greek noun.

who made heaven and earth.

but the earth He gave to the sons of men.

113:25The dead will not praise Thee, Lord,
nor any who descend into Hades,

113:26but we, the living, will bless the Lord
from now and for ever.

Psalms 117

Read this chapter on staging

117:1Hallelujah.
Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good,
for His mercy is for ever.

117:2Let the house of Israel now say that He is good,
that His mercy is for ever.

117:3Let the house of Aaron now say that He is good,
that His mercy is for ever.

117:4Let all those who fear the Lord now say that He is good,
that His mercy is for ever.

117:5In affliction I called upon the Lord,
and He answered me with room to breathe.

117:6The Lord is my helper;
I will not fear what a man will do to me.

117:7The Lord is my helper,
and I will look upon my enemies.

117:8Better to trust in the Lord
than to trust in a man.

117:9Better to hope in the Lord
than to hope in rulers.

117:10All nations surrounded me,
and in the name of the Lord I warded them off.

117:11Surrounding me, they surrounded me,
and in the name of the Lord I warded them off.

117:12They surrounded me like bees a honeycomb,
and they blazed up like fire among thorns,
and in the name of the Lord I warded them off.

117:13Pushed, I was overturned so as to fall,
and the Lord took hold of me.

117:14The Lord is my strength and my hymn,
and He has become my salvation.

117:15A voice of exultation and salvation is in the tents of the righteous:
“The Lord’s right hand has done a mighty work;

117:16the Lord’s right hand lifted me high;
the Lord’s right hand has done a mighty work.”

117:17I will not die, but live,
and tell in full the works of the Lord.

117:18The Lord disciplined me with discipline,
and did not hand me over to death.

117:19Open for me the gates of righteousness;
entering through them, I will give thanks to the Lord.

117:20This is the gate of the Lord;
the righteous will enter through it.

117:21I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me
and becamest my salvation.

117:22The stone the builders rejected—
this has become the head of the corner.

117:23This has come from the Lord,
and is marvelous in our eyes.

117:24This is the day the Lord has made;
let us exult and be glad in it.

117:25O Lord, save now!
O Lord, prosper us now!

117:26Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.
We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.

117:27The Lord is God, and He has shone upon us.
Arrange a festival among the thickly covering boughs,
up to the horns of the altar.

117:28Thou art my God, and I will thank Thee;
Thou art my God, and I will exalt Thee.
I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me
and becamest my salvation.

117:29Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good,
for His mercy is for ever.

Psalms 118

Read this chapter on staging

118:1Hallelujah.
One: Alph.
Blessed are the blameless in the way,
those who walk in the Lord’s law.

118:2Blessed are those who search out His testimonies;
with their whole heart they will seek Him.

118:3For those who practice lawlessness
did not walk in His ways.

118:4Thou didst command Thy commandments
to be kept diligently.

118:5If only my ways were directed
to keep Thine ordinances!

118:6Then I will certainly not be ashamed
when I look upon all Thy commandments.

118:7I will give thanks unto Thee, Lord, with uprightness of heart,
when I have learned Thy righteous judgments.

118:8I will keep Thine ordinances;
do not forsake me utterly.

118:9Two: Beth.
By what will the younger man set his way right?
By keeping Thy words.

118:10With my whole heart I sought Thee;
do not thrust me away from Thy commandments.

118:11In my heart I hid Thy sayings,
so that I might not sin against Thee.

118:12Blessed art Thou, Lord;
teach me Thine ordinances.

118:13With my lips I declared
all the judgments of Thy mouth.

118:14In the way of Thy testimonies I delighted,
as in all wealth.

118:15I will ponder Thy commandments
and consider Thy ways.

118:16I will meditate on Thine ordinances;
I will not forget Thy words.

118:17Three: Gimal.
Recompense Thy servant;
I will live and keep Thy words.

118:18Uncover my eyes,
and I will consider Thy wonders from Thy law.

118:19I am a sojourner on the earth;
do not hide Thy commandments from me.

118:20My soul longed to desire
Thy judgments at every time.

118:21Thou didst rebuke the arrogant;
accursed are those who turn away from Thy commandments.

118:22Remove reproach and contempt from me,
for I sought Thy testimonies.

118:23For rulers also sat and were speaking against me,
but Thy servant was pondering Thine ordinances.

118:24For Thy testimonies are also my meditation,
and Thine ordinances are my counsels.

118:25Four: Delth.
My soul clung to the ground;
give me life according to Thy word.

118:26I declared my ways, and Thou heardest me;
teach me Thine ordinances.

118:27Give me understanding of the way of Thine ordinances,
and I will ponder Thy wonders.

118:28My soul dripped away from weariness;
strengthen me by Thy words.

118:29Remove the way of injustice from me,
and show me mercy through Thy law.

118:30I chose the way of truth;
I did not forget Thy judgments.

118:31I clung to Thy testimonies;
Lord, do not put me to shame.

118:32I ran the way of Thy commandments
when Thou didst enlarge my heart.

118:33Five: Ē.
Instruct me, Lord, in the way of Thine ordinances,
and I will seek it continually.

118:34Give me understanding, and I will search out Thy law
and keep it with my whole heart.

118:35Guide me in the path of Thy commandments,
for I desired it.

118:36Bend my heart toward Thy testimonies,
and not toward greed.

118:37Turn away my eyes so that they do not see futility;
give me life in Thy way.

118:38Establish Thy saying for Thy servant,
for the fear of Thee.

118:39Remove my reproach, which I dreaded,
for Thy judgments are good.

118:40Behold, I desired Thy commandments;
give me life in Thy righteousness.

118:41Six: Ouau.
May Thy mercy also come upon me, Lord,

118:42And I will answer those who reproach me with a word,
for I hoped in Thy words.

118:43And do not remove the word of truth from my mouth utterly,
for I placed my hope in Thy judgments.

118:44And I will keep Thy law continually,
for ever and for the age of the age.

118:45And I was walking in a broad place,
for I sought Thy commandments.

118:46And I was speaking of Thy testimonies
before kings, and I was not ashamed.

118:47And I was meditating on Thy commandments,
which I loved greatly.

118:48And I raised my hands toward Thy commandments, which I loved,
and I was pondering Thine ordinances.

118:49Seven: Zai.
Remember Thy word to Thy servant,
upon which Thou didst cause me to hope.

118:50This comforted me in my humiliation,
for Thy saying gave me life.

118:51The arrogant were acting lawlessly to an extreme,
but I did not turn away from Thy law.

118:52I remembered Thy judgments from of old, Lord,
and I was comforted.

118:53Despondency seized me because of sinners
who forsake Thy law.

118:54Thine ordinances were songs to me
in the place of my sojourning.

118:55I remembered Thy name in the night, Lord,

118:56This came to be mine,
for I sought Thine ordinances.

118:57Eight: Ēth.
Thou art my portion, Lord;
I said that I would keep Thy law.

118:58I entreated Thy face with my whole heart;
have mercy on me according to Thy saying.

118:59I considered Thy ways
and turned my feet toward Thy testimonies.

118:60I was prepared and was not troubled
to keep Thy commandments.

118:61Sinners’ cords entangled me,
and I did not forget Thy law.

118:62At midnight I would rise to give thanks unto Thee
for Thy righteous judgments.

118:63I am a companion of all who fear Thee
and of those who keep Thy commandments.

118:64The earth is full of Thy mercy, Lord;
teach me Thine ordinances.

118:65Nine: Tēth.
Thou didst deal kindly with Thy servant,
Lord, according to Thy word.

118:66Teach me kindness, discipline and knowledge,
for I trusted Thy commandments.

118:67Before I was humbled, I did wrong;
therefore I kept Thy saying.

118:68Thou art good, Lord, and in Thy goodness
teach me Thine ordinances.

118:69The injustice of the arrogant multiplied against me,
but I will search out Thy commandments with my whole heart.

118:70Their heart curdled like milk,

118:71It is good for me that Thou didst humble me,
so that I might learn Thine ordinances.

118:72The law of Thy mouth is better for me

118:73Ten: Iōth.

118:74Those who fear Thee will see me and rejoice,
for I placed my hope in Thy words.

118:75I knew, Lord, that Thy judgments are righteousness,
and that in truth Thou didst humble me.

118:76Let Thy mercy now be for my comfort,
according to Thy saying to Thy servant.

118:77Let Thy compassions come to me, and I will live,
for Thy law is my meditation.

118:78Let the arrogant be ashamed, for they unjustly acted lawlessly against me;
but I will ponder Thy commandments.

118:79Let those who fear Thee turn to me,
and those who know Thy testimonies.

118:80Let my heart be blameless in Thine ordinances,
so that I may not be ashamed.

118:81Eleven: Chaph.
My soul fails with longing for Thy salvation,

118:82My eyes failed with longing for Thy saying,

118:83For I became like a wineskin in frost;

118:84How many are the days of Thy servant?

118:85Lawbreakers told me idle tales,
but not in keeping with Thy law, Lord.

118:86All Thy commandments are truth;

118:87They nearly brought me to an end on the earth,
but I did not forsake Thy commandments.

118:88Give me life according to Thy mercy,
and I will keep the testimonies of Thy mouth.

118:89Twelve: Labd.
For ever, Lord,
Thy word remains in heaven.

118:90Thy truth is from generation to generation;
Thou didst found the earth, and it remains.

118:91By Thine arrangement the day remains,
for all things are Thy servants.

118:92If Thy law had not been my meditation,
then I would have perished in my humiliation.

118:93I will certainly never forget Thine ordinances,
for by them Thou gavest me life, Lord.

118:94I am Thine; save me,
for I sought Thine ordinances.

118:95Sinners waited for me to destroy me;
I understood Thy testimonies.

118:96I saw an end to every completion;
Thy commandment is exceedingly broad.

118:97Thirteen: Mēm.
How I loved Thy law, Lord!
It is my meditation all day.

118:98Thou madest me wiser than my enemies in Thy commandment,
for it is mine for ever.

118:99I understood more than all who teach me,
for Thy testimonies are my meditation.

118:100I understood more than elders,
for I sought Thy commandments.

118:101I restrained my feet from every evil way,
so that I might keep Thy words.

118:102I did not turn away from Thy judgments,
for Thou didst instruct me.

118:103How sweet are Thy sayings to my throat,
beyond honey and honeycomb to my mouth!

118:104From Thy commandments I gained understanding;
therefore I hated every way of injustice,
for Thou didst instruct me.

118:105Fourteen: Noun.
Thy word is a lamp to my feet
and a light to my paths.

118:106I have sworn and established it:
to keep Thy righteous judgments.

118:107I was humbled to an extreme;
Lord, give me life according to Thy word.

118:108Please accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, Lord,
and teach me Thy judgments.

118:109My soul is in my hands continually,
and I did not forget Thy law.

118:110Sinners set a trap for me,
and I did not wander from Thy commandments.

118:111I inherited Thy testimonies for ever,
for they are my heart’s rejoicing.

118:112I bent my heart to perform Thine ordinances
for ever, for a recompense.

118:113Fifteen: Samch.
I hated lawbreakers,
and I loved Thy law.

118:114Thou art my helper and my upholder;
I placed my hope in Thy word.

118:115Turn away from me, evildoers,
and I will search out my God’s commandments.

118:116Uphold me according to Thy saying, and I will live;
and do not put me to shame in my expectation.

118:117Help me, and I will be saved;
and I will meditate on Thine ordinances continually.

118:118Thou didst despise all who depart from Thine ordinances,
for their thought is unjust.

118:119I reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors;
therefore I loved Thy testimonies continually.

118:120Nail down my flesh through fear of Thee,
for I feared Thy judgments.

118:121Sixteen: Ain.
I did judgment and righteousness;
do not hand me over to those who wrong me.

118:122Receive Thy servant for good;
do not let the arrogant oppress me with false accusations.

118:123My eyes failed with longing for Thy salvation
and for Thy righteous saying.

118:124Deal with Thy servant according to Thy mercy,
and teach me Thine ordinances.

118:125I am Thy servant; give me understanding,
and I will know Thy testimonies.

118:126It is time to act for the Lord;
they scattered Thy law.

118:127Therefore I loved Thy commandments
more than gold and topaz.

118:128Therefore I was set right toward all Thy commandments;
I hated every unjust way.

118:129Seventeen: Phē.
Thy testimonies are wonderful;
therefore my soul searched them out.

118:130The disclosure of Thy words will give light
and understanding to the simple.

118:131I opened my mouth and drew breath,
for I longed for Thy commandments.

118:132Look upon me and have mercy on me,
according to the judgment for those who love Thy name.

118:133Direct my steps according to Thy saying,
and let no lawlessness rule over me.

118:134Redeem me from people’s oppression through false accusation,
and I will keep Thy commandments.

118:135Shine Thy face upon Thy servant,
and teach me Thine ordinances.

118:136Streams of water ran down from my eyes,
since they did not keep Thy law.

118:137Eighteen: Sadē.
Thou art righteous, Lord,
and Thy judgment is upright.

118:138Thou didst command Thy testimonies as righteousness
and exceeding truth.

118:139Zeal for Thy house melted me away,
for my enemies forgot Thy words.

118:140Thy saying has been thoroughly refined by fire,
and Thy servant loved it.

118:141I am younger and despised;
I did not forget Thine ordinances.

118:142Thy righteousness is righteousness for ever,
and Thy law is truth.

118:143Affliction and constraint found me;
Thy commandments are my meditation.

118:144Thy testimonies are righteousness for ever;
give me understanding, and I will live.

118:145Nineteen: Kōph.
I cried with my whole heart; hear me, Lord;
I will seek Thine ordinances.

118:146I cried unto Thee; save me,
and I will keep Thy testimonies.

118:147I rose early at an untimely hour and cried out;
I placed my hope in Thy words.

118:148My eyes were awake before dawn
to meditate on Thy sayings.

118:149Hear my voice, Lord, according to Thy mercy;
give me life according to Thy judgment.

118:150Those who pursue me with lawlessness drew near,
but they were far from Thy law.

118:151Thou art near, Lord,
and all Thy commandments are truth.

118:152From the beginning I knew from Thy testimonies
that Thou didst establish them for ever.

118:153Twenty: Rēs.
See my humiliation and rescue me,
for I did not forget Thy law.

118:154Judge my case and redeem me;
give me life because of Thy word.

118:155Salvation is far from sinners,
for they did not seek Thine ordinances.

118:156Thy compassions are many, Lord;
give me life according to Thy judgment.

118:157Many are those who pursue me and press me hard;
I did not turn away from Thy testimonies.

118:158I saw those who break faith and melted away,
for they did not keep Thy sayings.

118:159See that I loved Thy commandments;
Lord, give me life in Thy mercy.

118:160The beginning of Thy words is truth,
and all Thy righteous judgments endure for ever.

118:161Twenty-one: Sen.
Rulers pursued me without cause,
and my heart was afraid of Thy words.

118:162I will rejoice in Thy sayings
like one who finds much spoil.

118:163I hated and abhorred injustice,
but I loved Thy law.

118:164Seven times a day I praised Thee
for Thy righteous judgments.

118:165Great peace belongs to those who love Thy law,

118:166I awaited Thy salvation, Lord,
and I loved Thy commandments.

118:167My soul kept Thy testimonies

118:168I kept Thy commandments and Thy testimonies,

118:169Twenty-two: Thau.
Let my supplication draw near before Thee, Lord;

118:170May my plea enter before Thee;

118:171May my lips pour forth a hymn

118:172May my tongue utter Thy saying,

118:173Let Thy hand be for saving me,

118:174I longed for Thy salvation, Lord,
and Thy law is my meditation.

118:175My soul will live and praise Thee,
and Thy judgments will help me.

118:176I wandered like a lost sheep;

Frost, curdled milk, additional clause in 104, plural paths, recompense, nail down my flesh, topaz, zeal for Thy house, beginning of words and seven times remain. Difficult 42, 120, 126, 128 and 136 require specialist syntax/referent review.

Read this chapter on staging

120:1A song of the ascents.
I lifted my eyes to the mountains.
From where will my help come?

120:2My help is from the Lord,
who made heaven and earth.

120:3Do not give your foot over to shaking,
and may your Keeper not slumber.

120:4Behold, the One guarding Israel
will neither slumber nor sleep.

120:5The Lord will guard you;

120:6By day the sun will not scorch you,

Psalms 136:9 · infant

Sense. The young children named in the violent closing imprecation.

Preserve the troubling literal object and the actions without euphemism. Place the line within the exilic lament and mark allegorical or spiritual readings as reception; they must not replace infants in the translation.

Historical comparison. KJV and DRC have little ones; Saints and Brenton infants. The source has a singular rock where KJV uses stones. The utterance is an imprecation within the poem.

Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek chapter · Lexical record carried forward from the Saints Biblical Lexicon, Wisdom review, 26 September 2026. Independent linguistic review remains outstanding.

The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Jerusalem/Babylon address uses you/your. Future will repay/will seize/dash follows the Greek futures in 8–9. Repeated empty her and repay/repayment, infants and singular rock retained without euphemism; the inherited note locates the imprecation in exilic lament.

Lord, Thy mercy is for ever;
do not neglect the works of Thy hands.
